title: 2027 Global Payments Analyst Program - Full time - Dublin
description: **Job Description** As a Global Payments Analyst, you will gain hands-on experience in the innovative landscape of global payments, learning what it takes to “make money move” and promote innovation across financial technology. The Global Payments Program at JPMorganChase offers the opportunity to build a career in the world of payments and financial technology—helping clients manage and move money locally, regionally and globally. Our Global Payments business brings together Payments, Merchant Services and Commercial Card, delivering end-to-end capabilities across the full Pay In and Pay Out lifecycle. Based in Ireland, you'll join a collaborative team that supports clients operating in Ireland and beyond, with exposure to global platforms, product innovation, and the partners who help deliver industry-leading cash management and payment solutions. You'll receive structured training, mentorship, and the chance to contribute to meaningful projects, while building a strong peer network and engaging with senior leaders. You'll work with teams that support local, regional and global clients—helping them manage liquidity and cash flow, pay suppliers, collect funds, accept payments, and optimize working capital through solutions spanning Pay In and Pay Out, Merchant Services, and Commercial Card. **Job Responsibilities** You will: * Begin learning how we support clients' cash management needs and technology-based payment solutions, from Ireland into wider regional and global corridors * Identify opportunities to leverage emerging technologies to meet evolving client needs * Gain exposure to product, implementation and client coverage teams across Global Payments (including Payments, Merchant Services and Commercial Card) * Contribute to developing ideas that improve the client experience and transform the payments landscape * Work under the guidance of mentors and a supportive team * Build your network through best-in-class training and access to business leaders, and learn how our businesses work together to deliver excellent customer service **Required Qualifications, Capabilities And Skills** We're looking for individuals with: * A keen interest in global payments / financial technology, with strong investigative, quantitative and analytical skills and attention to detail * Strong research, project management and communication skills * Ability to multi-task, solve problems and work under pressure * An energetic, confident approach and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative environment * Excellent written and oral communication skills in English, including the ability to prepare and deliver clear and concise written outputs * Working knowledge of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) * We accept applications from all degree disciplines; numerical confidence and familiarity with business fundamentals is helpful **Graduation date** April 2027 - August 2027 **Other Attributes/Characteristics** Demonstrable personal qualities, outside interests and achievements beyond academia that showcase the kind of person you are and the difference you could bring to the team. **About Us** J.P. Morgan is a global leader in financial services, providing strategic advice and products to the world's most prominent corporations, governments, wealthy individuals and institutional investors. Our first-class business in a first-class way approach to serving clients drives everything we do. We strive to build trusted, long-term partnerships to help our clients achieve their business objectives. We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. title: ARC School’s Project Facilitator
description: **Description of the Project** The Aquaculture Remote Classroom (ARC) has been developed by Bord Iascaigh Mhara as part of a European wide campaign, called #FarmedintheEU. The aim of this EU initiative is to raise awareness about aquaculture in Ireland and to promote the benefits of eating, buying, and selling sustainable seafood. The ARC travels around Ireland, delivering aquaculture workshops to primary schools. In addition, the ARC has developed online learning resources to support the long-term sustainability and success of the project. The ARC frequently participates in industry and public outreach events that are aligned to the project scope such as food festivals/college science weeks. Location: Travelling around the Republic of Ireland. Office base Dublin. Reporting Structure: H2 Learning, Louise Morgan, ARC Project Manager **Purpose of the role Description of the Project** The role of the Project Facilitator is to promote and deliver the programmes and resources offered by the BIM, Aquaculture Remote Classroom. The role will include delivering engaging and informative workshops, presentations and webinars to students using various in-person and online platforms. **Principle tasks** 1. To deliver the ARC programmes to primary and post-primary schools. 2. To jointly manage the schedule, logistics and administrative tasks associated with the role. 3. To manage the daily operations of the mobile unit (opening/closing/power/Wi-Fi/housekeeping/cleaning). 4. To manage the safety of pupils entering/exiting vehicle and while on board the vehicle. 5. To represent Bord Iascaigh Mhara at various industry related events, conferences, and public outreach events both in Ireland and Europe. 6. To maintain good working relationships with various stakeholders. **Essential Criteria** * Hold a relevant primary degree. * Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to work and contribute within a small team environment. * The ability to work unsupervised, with flexibility and with good initiative. * Willingness to complete Garda Vetting, Child Protection, First Aid and Manual Handling training. * A full clean driver’s licence and access to own transport, as the role will require regular travel. * Fluency in English and excellent communication skills. **Desirable Criteria** * A degree in science, marine biology, agricultural sciences, environmental science, geoscience, nutrition, or other relevant area is an advantage. * Knowledge of Seafood and Aquaculture. * Genuine interest in aquaculture and marine science communication. * Good personal organisational and priority setting skills, with the ability to manage a busy schedule. * Good interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to interact with individuals (young and professional) in a multidisciplinary environment. * Capable of working independently as well as being an effective team player, with initiative and enthusiasm. * Experience in collaborating, problem solving and values the sharing of information and continuous improvement within a professional environment. **Please note** * The role involves manual handling, and the physical setup, movement and storage of equipment and educational resources. The facilitator must be capable of safely carrying out these duties, including completing manual handling training and following relevant health and safety procedures. * This role involves regular travel and substantial time on the road, delivering workshops and supporting events across Ireland. The successful candidate must be willing to stay away from home overnight as required by the programme schedule. Travel and subsistence expenses, including overnight stays where required, will be paid at the applicable public sector rates. **Application Process** Applicants should submit a CV and short cover letter outlining their relevant expertise and experience regarding the above essential and desirable criteria. Send applications to: lmorgan@h2.ie Closing date: 30 th October 2026

title: Analyst, Restructuring
description: Our professionals balance analytical skills, deep market insight and independence to deliver solid, defensible analysis and practical advice to our clients. description: **About the role** We pride ourselves on offering customers the biggest range of products around. And that's not just food, but everything from clothes and kettles to financial services. These include but aren't limited to: * Competitive Salary * Bonus Scheme\* * Our Virtual GP service provides free and confidential access to an online GP through video GP consultations, and online prescription service for colleagues. The service is also available to families of colleagues who live at the same address for a reduced cost. * 24/7 access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) for you and family members for in the moment emotional support along with free access to a range of wellbeing services supporting you under our new Wellbeing First approach of Body, Mind and Life. * Colleague Clubcard offering 10% discount across stores and online, with 15% discount weekends once a month (Friday to Sunday), and 20% off twice a year. There is also 20% off F&F clothing, all year long, these various discounts can be extended to a family member with a 2nd Clubcard available.\* * Life Assurance * Pension Plan\* * Save As You Earn Scheme\* * Paid Family Leave * Bike to Work * Long Service Awards * Commuter Scheme * \*Entry requirements and rules of the scheme apply **About Us** Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer's favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move. Our core purpose is "Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day". Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers. It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children's Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food. We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards. We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated. description: **Minimum qualifications:** * Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience. * Experience with computer hardware and server hardware or troubleshooting/diagnosing. * Experience with operating systems and networking protocols. * Experience in project management and working with cross-functional stakeholders and leaderships. * Ability to participate in material handling tasks such as lifting, carrying or moving up to 50 lbs of equipment, the required use of safety equipment such as limited weight bearing work platforms, ladders, step stools and personal protective equipment (PPE) like safety harnesses in accordance with safety and ergonomic guidelines and assessments. **Preferred qualifications:** * Experience in maintenance and monitoring of server systems. * Experience working within a data center or network operation center environment. * Experience with Linux operating systems. * Ability to collaborate and partner with teams to overcome issues. * Ability to travel up to 20% of the time internationally. **About The Job** Google isn't just a software company. title: Graduate Programme, Audit - Dublin (Sept 2027)
description: **Job Description** **Why Start Your Career at S&W?** Starting your career is about more than just a job. It's about the people you learn from, the relationships you build and the experiences that shape you. Whether that's passing an exam, achieving a personal milestone or celebrating success with your colleagues, you'll be part of a team that's invested in your growth, celebrates your successes and supports you to be yourself. At S&W, you'll be given meaningful work from day one, while having the support, training and encouragement to help you succeed. You'll learn by doing, working alongside experienced colleagues, contributing to real projects and developing valuable professional skills from the start. As your confidence grows, so will your opportunities, with plenty of support along the way. As a growing accountancy and advisory firm, we offer a balance of opportunity and support. You'll learn from people at every level of the business, gain exposure to a variety of clients, industries and experiences, and develop the skills, knowledge and confidence needed to build a successful career. **The Audit & Assurance Team at S&W** Our Audit & Assurance team works with a diverse range of clients, from entrepreneurial and family-owned businesses to charities, not-for-profit organisations and larger established businesses across a variety of industries. What sets Audit & Assurance at S&W apart is the breadth of experience you'll gain early in your career. You'll develop technical expertise, commercial awareness and a well-rounded understanding of how organisations operate, while working closely with experienced colleagues and gaining exposure to senior leaders and Partners. Together, this provides a strong foundation for a successful career in the profession. **What Will You Be Doing?** As part of our Audit & Assurance team, you'll work alongside colleagues to deliver services to a variety of clients. You'll be involved in different stages of an engagement, gaining insight into how organisations operate and the role assurance plays in building confidence in financial reporting. Alongside your role, you'll study towards the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) or Chartered Accountants Ireland (CAI) qualification. Through a combination of professional training and practical experience, you'll build a strong foundation in audit, accountancy and wider business advisory services. You'll be supported with funded training, dedicated study time and guidance from colleagues who have successfully completed the qualification themselves. Your work will include: * Analysing financial information * Testing processes and controls * Building relationships with client teams * Resolving audit and accountancy queries * Supporting a range of audit and accountancy projects Whether you're based in one of our offices or working directly with clients, you'll contribute to meaningful work from day one while building the skills and confidence needed to become a trusted adviser. **To Be Successful in This Role** You'll be someone who: * Is curious, eager to learn and open to new challenges * Enjoys working with others and building positive relationships * Has a keen eye for detail and enjoys solving problems * Is proactive and looks for ways to make a positive contribution * Takes ownership of their development and is motivated to achieve their goals You'll also need to: * Be committed to working towards the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) or Chartered Accountants Ireland (CAI) qualification * Have some accountancy experience, as part of your education or work experience * Have obtained or be predicted a minimum 2:2 degree, in any discipline * Minimum 400 Leaving Certificate points (or equivalent) * Leaving Certificate O2 or H5 in Maths and English (or equivalent) **Your Learning & Development** We'll support you throughout your qualification journey with a leading UK training provider, dedicated study time and practical experience that complements your learning. You'll join as part of a cohort and benefit from a support network that includes experienced colleagues, a buddy and our Learning & Development team, helping you make the most of the opportunities available to you. **As a Colleague at S&W, You'll Have Access to Benefits That Include** * Fully funded training towards professional qualifications * Competitive salary * Private medical insurance * Life assurance * Pension contribution * Generous holiday package * Option to purchase additional holiday * Cycle to work scheme * Season ticket loan * Eye care support * Shared parental leave **Our Commitment to Inclusion** We are proud to value the differences that a diverse workforce brings, representative of society and our clients. At S&W we have a wide range of highly active employee resource groups and we’re delivering multiple diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives across the organisation. It is our commitment to provide a workspace where all colleagues, regardless of identity, background, or circumstance, feel respected as individuals and feel that they can achieve their full potential and work in a safe, supportive, and inclusive environment. We are happy to make any reasonable adjustments to accommodate for your needs throughout the application process. Please let your Recruiter know. **IMPORTANT NOTES FOR COMPLETING YOUR APPLICATION** When you click on the **'I'm interested'** button, you'll be taken to your profile page. We're currently updating it, but in the meantime: * We can only accept one application to any of our programmes in a recruitment season. If you're unsuccessful, you'll need to wait until the following recruitment season to reapply. * Under the **Resume (CV)** section, uploading a document is mandatory; however, it will not be formally reviewed.

description: See it differently You see the world through a unique lens and that’s exactly what we need. We embrace how you see things differently – it’s essential for creating a sustainable future. Arup is a global consultancy with advisory and technical expertise across more than 150 disciplines. We guide, plan and design the future of the built environment. Globally, each year we recruit hundreds of graduates and students who help us see things differently and solve the most complex challenges facing our clients, climate and communities. The Opportunity Are you passionate about cities, urban development, sustainability, transport, and creating places where people thrive? Join Arup's Early Careers Programme as a Graduate Strategy Consultant within our Cities, Planning & Design (CPD) team and help shape the future of communities, infrastructure, and sustainable development. As a Graduate Strategy Consultant, you will work with multidisciplinary teams to solve complex challenges facing cities and regions. You'll support the development of evidence-based strategies, policies, and plans that help clients deliver sustainable, resilient, and inclusive outcomes. **What You'll Do But Not Limited To** * Contribute to city, regional, and infrastructure strategy projects. * Analyse data, trends, and emerging challenges affecting communities and the built environment. * Work creatively to develop and assess opportunities to improve the way people live and move around cities and the built environment * Support stakeholder engagement, workshops, and strategic planning activities. * Develop reports, presentations, and recommendations for public and private sector clients. * Collaborate with planners, engineers, economists, designers, and sustainability specialists to deliver innovative solutions. Is this role right for you? For this opportunity, we are seeking the following qualifications, skills and attributes: * A Bachelor's degree (Level 8 or above), or studying towards a Master's degree in the following relevant disciplines: * Urban Planning * Geography * Economics * Public Policy * Environmental Science * Architecture * Civil Engineering * Sustainability * Business, Strategy, or a related discipline **We'd Also Like To See** * Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills. * Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement abilities. * A passion for sustainable, resilient, and people-centred cities. * An interest in policy, strategy, urban development, and the future of the built environment. * A collaborative mindset and enthusiasm for working within multidisciplinary teams. We advise that you apply early. **Closing Date:** 12 November 2026 **Eligibility** We're able to consider candidates who require an employment permit to work in Ireland, where the role and offered salary meet the Irish Government's eligibility criteria (for example, under the Critical Skills or General Employment Permit schemes). All Employment Permits are granted at the discretion of the Deciding Officer with offers contingent to obtaining the correct immigration to work and reside in Ireland." title: Kitchen porter at The Anglers Rest
description: We are looking for full and part time **Kitchen Porters** to join our great team. The Anglers Rest is one of Dublin's best known and inviting restaurants. We are located in the Strawberry beds near Castleknock and the Phoenix Park in Dublin 15. To prepare and present food to The Wright Group's standard, working safely and hygienically as part of the kitchen team at their unit. **Key Responsibilities** * Prepare, cook and present dishes to the standard set by the Head Chef and the unit's menu specification * Follow HACCP, food safety and allergen procedures at all times * Keep the section, equipment and storage areas clean, organised and compliant with food hygiene standards * Check stock levels for the section and report shortages to the Head Chef / Sous Chef * Support other sections during service as required, and assist with prep for the next service * Follow correct storage, labelling and rotation (FIFO) of all food items * Report any equipment faults, safety hazards or food safety concerns immediately **Requirements** * Relevant food safety / HACCP training (or willingness to complete on induction) * Previous kitchen experience appropriate to the role * Able to work a rotating shift pattern including evenings, weekends and bank holidays * Good understanding of food hygiene, allergen and manual handling requirements * Team player who can work calmly under pressure during service Join the kitchen team at one of The Wright Group's Irish venues, where great food and teamwork go hand in hand. title: Legal Assistant - Debt Recovery
description: **Carlisle Solicitors** is a dynamic and progressive Law Firm based in Dublin City Centre specialising in Commercial Litigation. We have a terrific team structure, a client-centric culture and have been paperless since 2008. If you are looking to boost you career and grow your skills then look no further. **Overview:** This role offers a fantastic opportunity for a self-motivated candidate to join the firm at a time of change for the legal profession in Ireland. The role will be responsible for supporting the Legal Team in actively managing daily workloads. You should have the ability to work in a challenging and dynamic environment with evolving priorities. This is a great opportunity for an enthusiastic candidate to work with a progressive and personable law firm. As part of a new phase of business growth and development, we are seeking an experienced Debt Recovery Legal Assistant. This role offers a fantastic opportunity for a self-motivated individual to join the firm. The role will have responsibility supporting a Solicitor and Legal Executive in the management of their file portfolios. **This varied role includes:** Ø Diary management Ø Court attendance for motions, assistance on hearings; Ø Liaising with clients Ø Digital Dictation Ø Support day to day activities such as admin tasks regarding incoming and outgoing post, scanning, allocating, filing; new file set up, demand letter, or assisting with mediation declaration, certificate of confirmation, declaration/endorsement of service, judgment papers, service of judgment, sheriff (all elements), registration if received with sheriff instruction, etc. **The successful candidate will:** * Hold a degree in Law (desirable but not essential) * A minimum of 6-12 months debt recovery experience in a legal firm (highly desirable) * Be available 5 days a week in the office – Monday to Friday from 8.30am to 5pm * Excellent written & verbal communication skills · Be a good team player and have a flexible attitude to work; · Have customer service skills and good telephone manner; · Good typing skills and the confidence to embrace best-in-class office technology · Be a motivated energetic self-starter, capable of working well under pressure; The rewards package will be very attractive to the right candidate, and we’ll take your track record and past successes into account when making you an offer. title: Medical Laboratory Aide Histopathology Lab
description: **Post Title:** Medical Laboratory Assistant **Post Status:** Permanent **Department:** Histopathology Laboratory **Location:** Beaumont Hospital & Affiliated Sites **Reports to:** Chief Medical Scientist or other nominated Manager **Salary:** Appointment will be made on the Medical Laboratory Aide Scale (€42,033 - €49,050) at a point in line with Government pay policy **Hours of work:** Full-Time, 39 hours per week **Closing Date:** 12.00 Noon on 22/10/2026 **Please note the hospital reserves the right to close the competition early should a substantial number of applications be received.** **Responsibilities** **Key Duties & Responsibilities:** The duties of the Medical Laboratory Assistant include appropriate duties assigned by the line manager. The general duties include, but are not limited to: * To engage in the logging in, labelling, centrifuging, and separation of specimens. If you receive such a request claiming to be from Beaumont Hospital, please do not respond and report to the recruitment department immediately** **Supplementary information:** **The Hospital** **www.beaumont.ie** **Management Unit:** www.beaumont.ie/hr **Other ( Please specify ):** **Informal Enquiries ONLY to:** **(Please note NO APPLICATIONS will be accepted via the Informal Email)** **Name:** Sinead Macken **Title:** Chief Medical Scientist, Histology Department **Email address:** sineadmacken@beaumont.ie A short listing exercise may be carried out on the basis of information supplied in your application. In the event of a high volume of applications additional shortlisting criteria may be utilised.

title: Professional Banking Practitioner 2027.
description: **IOB - Professional Banking Practitioner Apprenticeship 2027** * Why choose between work and study when you can do both? * Looking for a role that combines real work experience, professional development, and a recognised degree qualification? * Ready to develop valuable skills, grow your professional network, and shape your future career in banking? **Salary: €30,525** **Location:** The apprenticeship will be located in one of our Branches, Customer Engagement Centres or Head Office locations in Dublin or Co. Kildare. These locations include; * Airside, Swords, Co. Dublin * Naas, Co. Kildare * Leopardstown, Dublin 18 * AIB Branch – Dublin City Centre * AIB Branch – Dublin North * AIB Branch – Dublin South **Why Join the IOB Apprenticeship Programme?** **Earn while you learn** Combine paid work with part-time study over three years, gaining banking experience while completing a UCD BSc in Banking and Financial Services (NFQ Level 8). **How The Programme Works** Work at AIB, in one of our Retail teams, four days a week and attend IOB/UCD classes on-site or online one day a week, supported by practical experience, mentoring and learning resources. **Career opportunities** The programme is ideal for anyone interested in building a career in banking or finance, including customer service, operations, financial advice and business support. The programme is scheduled to commence in October 2027. Successful applicants will be required to become members of the Institute of Banking (IOB). Membership fees will be paid by AIB for the duration of the apprenticeship. **What You’ll Do** * Join AIB's Retail business and gain hands-on experience in a customer-facing banking environment. * Develop practical skills in customer service, operations, problem-solving and relationship building. * Build confidence in understanding customers' financial needs and supporting them with day-to-day banking services. * Participate in learning events, networking opportunities and professional development activities with fellow apprentices. * Progress your knowledge, skills and responsibilities throughout the programme while working towards your UCD degree qualification. * Successfully complete academic modules, workplace assessments and programme milestones over the three-year apprenticeship. **What You Will Bring** * A strong interest in developing a career in financial services. * A commitment to learning and personal development. * Strong communication and interpersonal skills. * A positive attitude and willingness to work as part of a team. * Applicants must be 18 years of age on or before 31 August 2027 and have the legal right to work in the Republic of Ireland. **Entry Requirements** Applicants must meet one of the programme entry pathways: * Leaving Certificate entry route. * QQI/FET/PLC Business Studies pathway. * Equivalent international qualification. * Mature applicant route for candidates aged 23+ with relevant work experience. * Applicants may apply while awaiting Leaving Certificate or PLC results. * Please review the full programme entry criteria on the IOB programme webpage before applying. * Where relevant, applicants must also meet the English language proficiency requirements and obtain an NUI exemption. Further details are available on the IOB programme webpage. **What's in it for you?** **Alongside Valuable Experience And Development Opportunities, You'll Enjoy** * A paid role with one of Ireland's leading retail banks. * A fully supported pathway to a UCD Level 8 degree. * Mentoring and coaching from experienced colleagues. * Valuable workplace experience from day one. * Opportunities to develop professional, technical and customer service skills. * IOB membership fees covered by AIB throughout the programme. * Healthcare Scheme * Employee Assistance Programme * Family Leave Options * Two Volunteer Days per Year * Market-leading Pension Scheme At AIB, our values guide how we work and how we support each other. We're looking for ambitious and motivated individuals who are ready to start their career journey while earning a qualification and gaining valuable workplace experience. **Eligibility And Equal Opportunities** Applicants must be resident in the Republic of Ireland and be fully authorised to work, or hold a valid work permit, for the full duration of the programme. Any offer of employment will be conditional upon satisfactory evidence of the right to work in the Republic of Ireland. AIB is an equal opportunities employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates and are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process. **Closing date:** Friday 29th January 2027

title: Professional Banking Practitioner Apprenticeship Programme
description: Post Date : 15-Oct-2026 Close Date : 29-Jan-2027 PTSB is one of Ireland's leading retail and SME banks, with an innovative range of products and services powered through an evolving digital landscape, our focus is centred on ensuring we deliver what our customers, colleagues and communities need to be successful. The Professional Banking Practitioner Apprenticeship Programme, in collaboration with the Institute of Banking (IOB), offers an exciting opportunity to launch your career in Financial Services. The programme combines practical workplace experience with academic learning, allowing you to earn a salary while working towards a recognised qualification. Over three years, you will gain hands-on experience in the Retail Banking function, advising customers and working alongside experienced professionals, all while studying for a Bachelor of Science (BSc) in Banking and Financial Services, accredited by UCD. Within the first year of the programme, you will complete the Qualified Financial Advisor (QFA) designation, providing a strong foundation for your career. The Programme combines meaningful workplace learning with academic study, you will graduate with a recognised qualification while gaining the skills, knowledge, and professional confidence to a build a successful career in Financial Services and Banking. Throughout the programme, you will be supported by a Line Manager, a dedicated Mentor and key contacts within the Institute of Banking (IOB). **Responsibilities:** * Work on-site either at your assigned PTSB branch or PTSB’s Digital & Direct team in St. Stephens Green Contact Centre four days per week and attend IOB/UCD classes, either in person or online, one day per week. * When you join you will attend a 4-week bootcamp with IOB. Following bootcamp completion, you will hold Accredited Product Advisor (APA) designation in Loans. PTSB induction will commence following the 4-week bootcamp. * Complete programme assessments and academic requirements throughout the apprenticeship. * Achieve the Qualified Financial Adviser (QFA) designation during Year 1 of the programme. * Progress towards a UCD-accredited BSc in Banking and Financial Services. * Carry out day-to-day responsibilities and contribute to your team’s objectives. * Gain exposure to Retail Banking and develop your customer, commercial, and financial services knowledge. * Support and advise customers with day-to-day banking queries and service needs. Learn how to identify customer needs and provide appropriate banking solutions. * Build knowledge across PTSB’s products and services. * Support colleagues in delivering excellent customer experiences, through thoughtful insights to PTSBs products and services and how they best support our customer’s needs. * Build professional relationships with colleagues and stakeholders across the organisation. * Identify opportunities for continuous improvement and enhanced customer experiences. * Support team, department and bank-wide initiatives as opportunities arise. **Requirements:** * You must be 18 years of age on or before 31st August 2027. * Leaving Certificate Entry Requirements: Applicants must have achieved, or be on track to achieve: A minimum of two H5 grades (Higher Level). Plus, a minimum of four O6/H7 grades in the remaining subjects. * Legally entitled to work in the Republic of Ireland without restriction\*\* for the duration of the programme (October 2027 – October 2030). \*\*Without restriction refers to candidates who: (i) will have a visa in place which will be valid for the entirety of the 36 months (3 years) duration of the programme without any change in permission type required; and (ii) do not require any financial sponsorship from PTSB for a work visa from October 2027 – October 2030. * You must be committed to completing the BSc in Banking and Financial Services while working with PTSB and committed to achieving the Qualified Financial Adviser (QFA) designation during Year 1 of the programme. * All apprentices who join the programme must have access to a personal laptop, Chromebook, or other compatible device for the duration for the programme. **This is a 3-year Fixed Term Contract based in the Dublin Region.** **Is this you?** Please apply online on our website or via the apply link for this role. Your application will be sent through to our Talent Acquisition team and they will be in touch regarding your application. We reserve the right to draw up a shortlist for interview. The Bank understands the importance of a consistent and relentless focus on championing diversity and inclusion. We aim to attract, recruit, and retain individuals with diverse backgrounds, skills, competencies and abilities to work collaboratively to enhance the service we provide to all of our customers and the communities we serve.

description: **Full Time, On-Site** **St. Margaret’s, Co. Dublin, K67 P7E5** **Thursday to Monday, 8:00am – 4:00pm** **About The Role** As a Supply Chain Coordinator, you'll play a key role in making sure our production team has everything they need, when they need it, and to the right quality. This is a hands-on, fast-paced role where no two days are the same. You'll be the person who helps spot issues, gets to the bottom of what has happened and works with suppliers and internal teams to get things back on track. Whether it's a late delivery, incorrect stock, a quality issue or a last-minute change, you'll need to stay calm under pressure, communicate clearly and find a practical solution. You'll work closely with Production, Procurement, Warehouse, Product and FSQA teams, as well as our suppliers, to keep things moving and prevent the same issues from happening again. We're looking for someone who enjoys being the person others turn to when something needs fixing. You don't need to come from a traditional Supply Chain background - what's most important is your ability to take ownership, solve problems and get things done. **Who You Are** We're less concerned about having a specific Supply Chain background and more interested in **how you work** . You might come from Supply Chain, Production, Operations, Logistics, Customer Service, Retail, Hospitality or another fast-paced environment where you've had to deal with people, problems and competing priorities. **What Matters Is That You** * Are a natural problem-solver who enjoys figuring things out when things don't go to plan. * Take ownership and initiative - you see something that needs doing and get on with it. * Stay calm and focused when you're under pressure or dealing with unexpected problems. * Are confident having difficult or challenging conversations when needed, while maintaining positive working relationships. * Communicate clearly and are comfortable working with different stakeholders, including suppliers and teams on the production floor. * Are practical and hands-on — you're happy to get involved and understand what's happening on the ground rather than only working from behind a desk. * Can make sensible decisions independently and know when to ask for support. * Are organised and able to manage multiple priorities in a busy environment. * Have a strong 'get things done' mentality and don't need constant direction. * Are curious and naturally look for ways to improve how things work. * Are comfortable working in an environment where priorities can change quickly. * Are confident using basic systems and tools such as Excel, email and communication platforms. Experience with WMS, ERP or other data systems is helpful but not essential. * Previous Supply Chain, Operations, Production or related experience is useful, but not essential. A relevant qualification is also a plus rather than a requirement. **What You Will Be Doing** * Monitoring stock, deliveries and production requirements to help ensure we have the right products available at the right time. * Responding to day-to-day supply and delivery issues, quickly identifying what has gone wrong and taking action to resolve them. * Acting as a key point of contact for suppliers, building strong working relationships and confidently following up when things don't go to plan. * Working closely with Production, Procurement, Warehouse, Product and FSQA to communicate issues, agree actions and keep everyone aligned. * Managing multiple priorities at once, knowing what needs your attention first and staying organised in a fast-moving environment. * Investigating issues such as late or incorrect deliveries, oversupply and short shelf life, understanding the root cause and putting actions in place to prevent repeat problems. * Managing issues through to resolution, keeping relevant stakeholders updated and minimising any impact on production and our customers. * Monitoring supplier performance and feeding back on recurring issues, process compliance and opportunities for improvement. * Sharing information and learnings with the wider team and contributing to better ways of working. * Taking ownership of problems from start to finish rather than waiting for someone else to solve them. * Continuously looking for practical ways to improve processes, reduce waste and make day-to-day operations run more smoothly. **What We Offer** * 70% off HelloFresh + free shipping * Company Pension (matched 1:1 contributions up to 5%) * Health insurance * Annual Gym membership or Wellness benefit * Membership to global leading mindfulness App -
